article.title: Why a Significant A/B Test Result Can Still Be Too Small to Matter
article.why: Practical analytical English for data-driven decisions.

paragraphs.en: An A/B test can produce a statistically significant result and still have little practical value. Statistical significance addresses a specific question: if there were no true difference under the model assumptions, how surprising would the observed result be? It does not tell the business whether the effect is large enough to justify implementation. Suppose a campaign increases conversion from 10.00 percent to 10.10 percent. With millions of observations, that small difference may have a very low p-value. Yet the absolute lift is only 0.10 percentage points. Whether that matters depends on incremental conversions, margin per conversion, contact cost, implementation cost, customer experience, and operational capacity. The opposite situation also occurs. A test may show an economically interesting lift but fail to reach conventional statistical significance because the sample is small or the outcome is rare. In that case, the confidence interval is often more informative than a binary significant or not significant label. It shows the range of effect sizes reasonably compatible with the data under the assumptions. Business evaluation should therefore combine statistical uncertainty with economic consequences. Translate the estimated effect into incremental outcomes and value. For a mailing campaign, calculate additional conversions, incremental gross margin, delivery cost, and expected net contribution. For a product experiment, consider retention, support burden, latency, or other guardrail metrics. Predefining a minimum detectable effect or minimum practically important effect can also improve experiment design. It forces the team to ask before the test what size of improvement would actually change a decision. Multiple testing is another concern. If a team checks many metrics, segments, and time windows, some significant results can appear by chance. Primary outcomes and analysis rules should be specified in advance where possible. The final conclusion should avoid treating the p-value as a business score. A better statement is: “The estimated lift is 0.10 percentage points, the confidence interval excludes zero, but expected incremental profit is below the implementation threshold.” That sentence separates evidence about existence from evidence about usefulness. Statistical significance can support a decision, but it cannot make the decision by itself. Analysts should document the population, observation window, assumptions, and operational definition before drawing a conclusion. A useful review separates the observed metric from the mechanism that may have produced it and from the action that should follow. This discipline makes the result easier to reproduce, challenge, and communicate to stakeholders. paragraphs.zh: 繁中完整翻譯與解說：本文的核心不是只看表面指標，而是先確認母體、分母、時間範圍與選擇機制，再判斷數字是否真的代表 business outcome 改善。分析時要區分觀察事實、可能機制與因果結論，並把不確定性、經濟價值與下一步 action 一起納入。
paragraphs.ja: 日本語完全訳・解説：表面的なmetricだけで結論を出さず、母集団、分母、期間、selection mechanismを確認したうえでbusiness outcomeの改善を判断する。観察事実、考えられるmechanism、因果的な結論を分け、不確実性、経済価値、次のactionまで含めて説明することが重要である。
